$comment: The validator's warnings the gate accepts (0005), each by the message id the validator gives it and with the reason it is accepted rather than fixed. Any other warning refuses the resource that raised it, as an error does; a warning the validator gives no id cannot be registered and must be fixed. An entry that no resource of the corpus raised in a run fails the gate too, so an entry never outlives its reason. An entry accepts its id wherever the corpus raises it, not only where its reason says (0006 names that cost). Read by scripts/validator.mjs; held by scripts/validator/judge.test.mjs.

warnings.reason: dom-6, 'A resource should have narrative for robust management', a best-practice constraint. No resource here carries a narrative but a document's Composition, whose narrative of its titles CH ORF requires (0009). 0006 decides that a Questionnaire is written without one: its items are what a renderer shows, and a narrative made from them would be a second rendering of the same texts that could disagree with them and that nothing here checks. The same holds of every other resource the packages write that dom-6 asks of -- the QuestionnaireResponse, the DocumentReference, and health-ch's Patient, Practitioner, Organization, PractitionerRole and ServiceRequest, none of whose profiles makes text 1..1 (R4's, ch-orf-questionnaireresponse, ch-orf-servicerequest and CH Core's four, each text 0..1, read on 17 October 2026): a narrative made of a person's values would be a second rendering of them that nothing here checks against them, and a receiver renders the resources (0008, 0009).

Questionnaire.language, a BCP 47 tag such as de-CH, which the validator cannot validate in full offline: 'Resolved system urn:ietf:bcp:47 (v2.0.1), but the definition doesn't include any codes, so the code has not been validated' (measured with -tx n/a, 0005). A tag it cannot read at all -- de_CH, de-ch, zz -- is an error instead, not this warning (measured in review, 0006). A translation's language, the translation extension's lang, is information there, not a warning. A Questionnaire of a form with catalogues says its language, so every translated export raises it. health-core's language() holds the tag to its form and canonical case; whether its subtags are registered nothing here checks.

sdc-3, 'Semver is the preferred version algorithm', a best-practice constraint. formancy numbers a form's published versions 1, 2, 3 (its server's form_versions.version), which the integer algorithm orders exactly; written as semver, 3.0.0 would claim major, minor and patch meanings formancy's numbers do not have (0006).

gln-startswith76, CH Core 6.0.0's 'GLN must start with 76 for Swiss HCP', a warning (ch-core-gln-identifier, Identifier.value). The corpus's GLNs are under GS1's prefix 952, 'used for demonstrations and examples of the GS1 system' (GS1 General Specifications 26.0, Table 1-4), so that no organisation or person holds them, which scripts/synthetic-identifiers.test.mjs holds; and health-ch takes a GLN that does not start 76 -- the author's, who may practise outside Switzerland -- as the GLN it is (0009). Accepted wherever the corpus raises it, as every entry here is; a GLN that starts 76, as a Swiss practitioner's does, is in no corpus file, since nothing shows of one that nobody holds it.
